name: Tofacitinib for alopecia

card.summary: An oral JAK inhibitor prescribed off-label by some dermatologists to regrow scalp, brow and body hair lost to alopecia areata.
card.note: Prescription-only; carries an FDA boxed warning for infections, cancer and clotting.

quick.overview:
Tofacitinib (Xeljanz) is a prescription Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor approved for rheumatoid arthritis, ulcerative colitis and some other inflammatory conditions. Dermatologists have also used it off-label for alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition in which immune attack on hair follicles causes patchy or total hair loss.

For people with alopecia areata the appearance payoff is regrowth of scalp hair, eyebrows and lashes. The Cochrane review of alopecia areata treatments covers small molecule inhibitors among other options, and newer JAK inhibitors have since been approved specifically for the condition.
quick.how: It is taken as a prescribed oral medicine under specialist supervision, with blood monitoring. People who use it describe regrowth over months and discuss what happens when treatment stops. It is not an over-the-counter hair product and is not used for ordinary pattern hair loss.
quick.risks: Common effects listed include upper respiratory infections, headache, diarrhea and nasopharyngitis. The FDA boxed warning covers serious infections, lymphoma and other cancers, and, from 2019, blood clots and death at the higher dose, based on a rheumatoid arthritis safety trial. Live vaccines are to be avoided.

lead: Tofacitinib is an oral JAK1/JAK3 inhibitor, first approved in the US in November 2012 for rheumatoid arthritis and later for ulcerative colitis, juvenile arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis [1]. It is sold as Xeljanz and, in the EU, as the generic Inijaq [1].

Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease that causes non-scarring hair loss on the scalp or body [2]. Because JAK signalling carries inflammatory cytokine messages inside immune cells, tofacitinib has been used off-label to try to restore hair, brows and lashes in people with extensive disease. The appearance goal is regrowth of lost hair.

Three JAK inhibitors have since been authorised in the US specifically for severe alopecia areata: baricitinib (June 2022), ritlecitinib (June 2023) and deuruxolitinib (July 2024) [3]. Tofacitinib itself has no alopecia approval.

chain: Blocks JAK signalling in immune cells
Dampens immune attack on hair follicles
Hair regrows on scalp, brows and lashes
angle.text: For people with alopecia areata, tofacitinib is used to restore hair that the immune system has stopped follicles from producing. It does not target pattern (androgenetic) hair loss.

paras: Approved uses are rheumatoid arthritis, ulcerative colitis (the first oral drug the FDA approved for chronic ulcerative colitis, in May 2018), polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis [1]. Use in alopecia areata is off-label.

Treatments for alopecia areata include immunosuppressants, hair growth stimulants and contact immunotherapy, and the Cochrane network meta-analysis of randomised trials assessed short-term regrowth of at least 75% and serious adverse events across them, including small molecule inhibitors [4]. Wikipedia notes that for baricitinib 32% of people with 50% hair loss reached 80% scalp coverage at 36 weeks [3].

Common effects are upper respiratory infections, headache, diarrhea and nasopharyngitis. Serious effects include infections, malignancies and pulmonary embolism. The FDA boxed warning covers infections, lymphoma and other malignancies, and a 2019 boxed warning added blood clots and death at the higher dose [1].

A randomised safety trial in rheumatoid arthritis patients aged 50 or older with a cardiovascular risk factor found higher incidences of major cardiovascular events and cancers with tofacitinib than with a TNF inhibitor [5]. Live vaccines should be avoided, and dosing is reduced with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors [1].

Tofacitinib blocks JAK1 and JAK3, interrupting the JAK-STAT pathway that relays cytokine signals to the cell nucleus [1][6]. JAK3 has a central role in signalling that governs lymphocyte survival, proliferation and differentiation [6].

The Cochrane network meta-analysis of alopecia areata treatments evaluated randomised trials of immunosuppressants, small molecule inhibitors, contact immunotherapy and others [4]. The 2022 trial of tofacitinib cardiovascular and cancer risk was in rheumatoid arthritis, not hair loss [5].

timeline.event: FDA approves tofacitinib for rheumatoid arthritis [1].
Approved for ulcerative colitis in the US [1].
FDA boxed warning on clots and death at the higher dose [1].
Baricitinib becomes the first JAK inhibitor authorised for severe alopecia areata in the US [3].
